claim_text: The same report also recorded more hyperglycemia, stomatitis or mucosal inflammation, diarrhea, ocular events, and dose interruptions with inavolisib, even though discontinuation of inavolisib for adverse events was 6.8 percent `pmid-40454641`.
evidence_summary: INAVO120 final overall-survival report randomized PIK3CA-mutated HR-positive HER2-negative advanced breast cancer to inavolisib or placebo with palbociclib-fulvestrant; safety results showed higher hyperglycemia, stomatitis or mucosal inflammation, diarrhea and ocular toxic effects, more inavolisib dose interruptions, and 6.8 percent inavolisib discontinuation from adverse events. Limitation is regimen-specific toxicity in a selected first-line endocrine-resistant population.
reviewer_notes: Supported by abstract and safety section.

claim_text: In the prospective PRAEGNANT real-world cohort, 57 patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer received alpelisib plus fulvestrant, 55 after prior CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy; median PFS was 5.0 months and median OS was 20.1 months, with discontinuation mainly due to tumor progression and documented hyperglycemia, rash, and diarrhea `pmid-41925922`.
evidence_summary: Prospective German PRAEGNANT registry analysis included 57 HR-positive HER2-negative advanced breast cancer patients receiving alpelisib plus fulvestrant, with 55 previously exposed to CDK4/6 inhibitors; it reported median PFS of 5.0 months, median OS of 20.1 months, progression as the main discontinuation reason, and common AEs including hyperglycemia, skin toxicity or rash, and diarrhea. Limitation is real-world AE underreporting and small subgroups.
reviewer_notes: Supported; 'rash' corresponds to skin toxicity/rash wording in the paper.

claim_text: The study found maximum tolerated alpelisib doses for continuous and intermittent schedules, but grade 3 or higher gastrointestinal and electrolyte toxicities were frequent, and only 1 of 17 assessed patients had a partial response `pmid-33947692`.
evidence_summary: Phase I HER2-positive PIK3CA-mutant metastatic breast cancer triplet trial established alpelisib MTDs of 250 mg daily and 350 mg 4-days-on/3-days-off with trastuzumab and LJM716; grade 3 or higher diarrhea, hypokalemia, and hypomagnesemia were frequent, and among 17 response-assessed patients only one partial response occurred. Limitation is small safety-focused phase I design.
reviewer_notes: Supported by abstract, safety/dose-finding, and efficacy sections.

claim_text: Alpelisib plus aromatase inhibitor therapy produced clinical benefit in a phase I/II HR-positive metastatic breast cancer cohort, but paired tumor and ctDNA analyses showed PTEN loss-of-function events and ESR1 expansion that could explain resistance to either the PI3Kalpha or endocrine component `pmid-32864625`.
evidence_summary: Phase I/II alpelisib plus letrozole or exemestane study in HR-positive metastatic breast cancer reported clinical benefit among evaluable patients and used paired tumor/ctDNA profiling to identify PTEN loss-of-function alterations and ESR1 mutant allele expansion linked to progression; limitation is small non-comparator translational cohort.

claim_text: By contrast, functional-screen work with BYL719 and PIM kinases gained clinical relevance from paired biopsies, yet the authors explicitly described the biopsy analysis as preliminary because only a small number of paired treatment-naive and post-relapse samples were available `pmid-27604488`.
evidence_summary: BYL719 gain-of-function screen identified PIM kinases as resistance drivers maintaining downstream PI3K effector activity and evaluated paired clinical biopsies before treatment and after relapse; the authors treated the biopsy component as preliminary because the paired sample set was small. Limitation is limited clinical confirmation after strong functional screening.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the screen and paired-biopsy discussion.

claim_text: They note that post-CDK4/6 evidence is heterogeneous across trial design, biomarker criteria, endpoints, and control arms `pmid-42351448` `pmid-33976551`; that only some PI3K inhibitor biomarker findings are established while many combination biomarkers remain exploratory `pmid-31859350`; that ER-targeted therapy may remain biologically relevant in CDK4/6-resistant preclinical models `pmid-31852484`; and that ctDNA can guide selection but does not, by itself, prove a survival benefit for every genomically directed choice `pmid-39839709`.
evidence_summary: The cited reviews describe heterogeneous post-CDK4/6 trial designs, populations, biomarkers, endpoints, and sequencing evidence; the PI3K biomarker review distinguishes established PIK3CA predictive evidence from exploratory biomarkers; elacestrant preclinical work shows ER targeting retains activity in CDK4/6-resistant models; and PRAEGNANT ctDNA testing influenced treatment decisions without randomized survival testing. Limitations are review-level synthesis, preclinical ER evidence, and nonrandomized ctDNA clinical impact.
reviewer_notes: Supported as an interpretive synthesis of context and preclinical evidence, not as primary proof for every treatment choice.
